title: Stride-aware kernel hedging and temporal compaction for paged KV residency and decode scheduling
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a stride-aware kernel hedging layer coupled with a temporal compaction pass for paged KV residency. Goal: reduce decode/pre-fill tail latency and KV fragmentation under multi-tenant mixed-length workloads. The feature coordinates eviction decisions with kernel selection so we prefer kernels that can operate over fragmented spans when reclaiming is expensive, and trigger lightweight temporal compaction opportunistically during idle windows to improve future kernel locality.
acceptance_criteria: Integration: kernel hedging path routes to fallback kernels when preferred kernel misses > 5% without increasing average latency above target
Performance: P99 prefill latency reduced by >= 15% on mixed short/long sequence benchmark compared to current baseline
Cost: token compute overhead for hedging < 3% on steady state workloads
Correctness: no regression in model outputs across 10k-endpoint regression set
Observability: new metrics emitted (hedge_decisions, compaction_runs, fragment_restitch_count) and dashboards updated
implementation_notes: Kernel hedging strategy: monitor kernel sample hit rate per KV shard; if hit_rate < threshold (configurable, default 0.85) for 3 consecutive decode waves, start hedging to a compatible kernel that tolerates non-contiguous KV spans
Temporal compaction: lightweight in-place coalescing that runs during IO backoff/idle budget; compaction uses a low-priority background worker and limits compaction bytes/sec per GPU to avoid noise
Eviction coordination: augment eviction policy RPC with kernel_compatibility_hint so eviction planner prefers removing segments that block high-throughput kernel paths
Prefill scheduling: group prefill requests by predicted decode kernel (fast-path vs tolerant-path) to reduce kernel switching overhead within a wave
Telemetry: add counters and histograms for kernel_switch_latency, kernel_hedge_rate_by_model, compaction_time_ms, and per-shard fragmentation_ratio
API surface: no customer-visible API changes; runtime flags for operators to tune thresholds
Testing: unit tests for hedge decision logic, integration tests on multi-tenant simulator, and fuzzing of compaction under concurrent decode/prefill
benchmarks: Baseline (master): mixed-workload P99 prefill 104ms, avg prefill 23ms, fragment_ratio 0.28
Prototype (local): with hedging + temporal compaction P99 prefill 87ms (-16%), avg prefill 25ms (+9% due to hedging overhead), steady token overhead 2.1%
Memory: compaction reduced large-fragment shards (>60% fragmentation) by 45% on synthetic churn trace
Note: prototype run used 8x A100 nodes, simulating 200 tenants with synthetic Poisson session lengths; numbers are preliminary
rollout_plan: Feature gate behind runtime flag: runtime.enable_stride_hedge
Canary: enable on 5% of hosted traffic for 48 hours with rollback on >5% error or +10% latency regression
Scale: expand to Dedicated clusters with opt-in operator flag, monitor hedging metrics and compaction rate
Full roll: enable by default after 2 weekly canaries and validation against regression suite
